newsitem.title: UK: US insurance agents to lose auto mkt share - report.
newsitem.headline: US insurance agents to lose auto mkt share - report.

text.p: Insurance agents in the U.S. will lose market share in personal auto, maintain their position in home-owners and continue to dominate commercial property casualty, management consultant Datamonitor said.

"Personal auto insurance is largely viewed as a commodity. Consumers choose on price and the agent is perceived as adding little extra value," Datamonitor said in its report 'The Future of the US insurance agent 1996'.

In home-owners insurance, agents will maintain their market share at 35.9 percent at least until 2000 after a period of decline, boosted in part by the recognition of their local knowledge in the wake of disasters such as Hurricane Andrew and the Northridge earthquake.

"The agent has considerable local knowledge which can greatly benefit underwriting procedures. In the long-term, independent agents may even grow their market share," the report said. Finally, in the commercial property casualty (P&C) market, Datamonitor said agents, who have 71 percent market share, were in a secure position.
"This type of insurance is a more specialised complex area than personal lines...the commercial client often requires a far higher level of personal service and tailored solutions."
